title: Does the Heart Show Your Pain? Tackling the X-ITE Pain Challenge with Self-Supervised ECG Representation Learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.14662v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Accurate recognition of pain using physiological signals remains a challenging problem due to pain's subjective nature and high inter-individual variability. In this study, we investigate self-supervised representation learning (SSL) methods applied to unimodal electrocardiogram (ECG), complemented by multimodal pretraining, including accelerometer (ACC) signals from the chest. We focus on classifying low versus medium pain levels on the X-ITE Pain dataset. Our results reveal that while ECG-based models show limited classification performance, multimodal pretraining improves learned representations by capturing cross-modal dependencies. Notably, we observe substantial inter-subject variability in model performance, suggesting that pain-related ECG patterns may be subject-specific. translated_title: 心脏能否展现你的疼痛？利用自监督心电图表示学习应对X-ITE疼痛挑战
translated_abstract: 利用生理信号准确识别疼痛仍是一个具有挑战性的问题，因为疼痛具有主观性且个体间差异显著。在本研究中，我们探讨了将自监督表示学习方法应用于单模态心电图，并结合包括胸部加速度计信号在内的多模态预训练。我们专注于在X-ITE疼痛数据集上区分低度与中度疼痛水平。结果表明，虽然基于心电图的模型分类性能有限，但多模态预训练通过捕捉跨模态依赖关系改善了学习到的表示。值得注意的是，我们观察到模型性能存在显著的受试者间差异，这表明与疼痛相关的心电图模式可能具有个体特异性。可视化结果显示存在明显的受试者特异性聚类，但疼痛水平之间没有清晰分离，这凸显了从心电图中检测疼痛的复杂性。
tldr: 本研究通过自监督心电图表示学习及多模态预训练，发现疼痛识别受个体差异影响显著，心电图模式呈受试者特异性，难以直接区分疼痛水平。
en_tdlr: This study applies self-supervised ECG representation learning with multimodal pretraining, revealing that pain recognition is heavily subject-specific, with ECG patterns clustering by individual rather than by pain level.
